message:
proof(second-brain): freeze S1 gap inventory and S2 clause denominator

S1 reproduces the architecture-time machine-contract evidence gap:
0 MACHINE_CONTRACT hits for any ADR-named type, schemas/second_brain/
absent, 29 hits all PROSE_ONLY. Finding:
NO_SUFFICIENT_SECOND_BRAIN_MACHINE_CONTRACT_SET.

S2 freezes the coverage denominator at 97 clauses across 10 ADRs, every
clause bound to verbatim fragments of the ratified candidate
e4b28946...; 28 SB-DEC references match the candidate exactly and
SB-DEC-026 remains unlinked.

Committed before any contract artifact exists so that git history, not a
self-asserted field, proves the freeze preceded authoring.

ADR_CLAUSE_INVENTORY.json sha256
= f073ca28802e6b140dd5789d5fad5839962635f7b287cac589ec704efc663288

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(second-brain): machine contracts for ADR acceptance evidence (AC#2)

Closes the architecture-time machine-contract evidence gap reproduced in
S1. Amended acceptance condition #2 requires that 'machine contracts
required by this ADR MUST parse and cover the decision at ADR
acceptance'; before this change nothing existed for it to parse.

Adds under schemas/second_brain/contracts/:
  - adr-machine-contract.schema.json / interface-contract.schema.json
    meta-schemas. Frozen authority (candidate sha256, ratification
    binding, runtime_claims_permitted=false, denial-fixture status) is
    const-pinned, so a contract asserting runtime authority fails schema
    validation rather than convention.
  - ADR-SB-001..010.contract.json — 97 decision clauses, each a
    structured machine rule (subject/rule_type/operator/machine_value)
    bound to verbatim fragments of the ratified candidate e4b28946...
  - typed artifacts the ADRs name directly: LocalSpoolPort, CustodyPort,
    OpenLoopCandidate, TaskProposal, TaskPromotionRequest,
    ProjectIdentityEnvelope, ServiceCapabilityReceipt.
  - ADR_CONTRACT_COVERAGE.json — 97/97 COVERED, 0 MISSING, 0 AMBIGUOUS,
    hash-bound to the denominator frozen in the preceding commit.

Adds scripts/governance/validate_second_brain_adr_contracts.py: 113
fail-closed checks in two groups. Beyond structural validation it pins
the values that carry the architecture decision, because a purely
structural pass green-lights a contract with the right shape and the
wrong content.

Adds tests/governance/test_second_brain_adr_contracts.py: 46 tests
executing the real validator against mutated repository copies. Each
negative test asserts the specific guard responsible fires, not merely
that something failed. Semantic mutations are applied consistently
across inventory and contract so the cross-file agreement check cannot
take the credit for a semantic guard.

Also reconciles fo-01-repair-status.json against the later
FO01_RESOLUTION_RECEIPT.json. The two records on main disagreed about
whether FO-01 still blocked ADR acceptance; the receipt is later and
supersedes. FO-01 gate eligibility is recorded separately from
acceptance authorization, which remains false and operator-only.

No ADR is accepted; all ten remain PROPOSED. No runtime, implementation,
or enablement claim is made or authorized. Denial fixtures remain an
implementation-time gate and are explicitly not implemented.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

proof(second-brain): task packet, validation receipts, and handoff

Task packet validates against dopetask-canonical-spec.json (repo_marker
.dopetaskroot; executable steps pin the base SHA and leave --head
unpinned, so successor commits do not invalidate the step).

Receipts record what actually ran: validator 113 checks / 0 failed,
adversarial matrix 46/46, change-contract preflight PASS at max_lane L2
over 29 paths, git diff --check clean, pre-commit 4 passed / 14 skipped
with the skips verified against .pre-commit-config.yaml rather than
assumed.

Every NOT_RUN bucket is recorded as NOT_RUN. Contract coverage is
architecture-time evidence and is not collapsed into runtime evidence.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(second-brain): close a real validator false-green via value grounding

The 46-test adversarial matrix passed, so I attacked the validator
itself rather than trusting that. Group S pins ~37 of 97 clauses; the
other ~60 had no pinned semantic guard.

Demonstrated false-green: editing the inventory AND the contract
consistently rerouted ADR-SB-002-C01 canonical capture from Dope-Memory
to ConPort — a genuine architecture change — and the validator still
exited 0 with 113/113. Every guard survived it: the cited fragment was
untouched so it remained a real candidate substring with a matching
hash, both sides were edited so cross-file agreement held, and ConPort
is a legitimate member of the closed authority set.

Adds check A21 (value grounding): for canonical authority routing
(AUTHORITY_TARGET/EQUALS), closed policy enums (ENUM/SET_EQUALS) and
numeric bounds, the machine value must itself appear in the decision
text the clause cites. Kept deliberately narrow — SUPERSET_OF is
excluded because a contract may legitimately normalise a term the prose
abbreviates, and a grounding rule that is sometimes wrong is worse than
none.

Six new tests cover this class, including two clauses with no pinned
Group-S guard that grounding alone catches.

114 checks / 0 failed; 52 adversarial tests / 0 failed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

proof(second-brain): independent audit FAIL — BLOCKED_INDEPENDENT_AUDIT

Independent read-only audit of frozen head 7955ef33d7 returned FAIL with
3 blockers and 5 must-fix. Packet requires PASS with zero of each, so
publication does not progress: PR #1227 stays a draft.

Producer re-derived all three blockers from repository bytes rather than
accepting them on assertion, and disputes none:

- B1 the coverage PASS survives silent architecture rewrites. Editing
  inventory and contract consistently changes a decision while the
  validator exits 0, on ~75 of 97 clauses. A21 narrowed this class; it
  did not close it.
- B2 'dopeTask' is an invented canonical authority. grep -c against the
  candidate returns 0; the token came from this packet's own boundary
  list, not the ratified candidate.
- B3 A21 enum grounding is one-way. It rejects widening but accepts
  shrinking: dropping PURGE from the deletion set and Review from the UX
  set both still pass.

MUST_FIX 1 is the consequential one: the denominator, derived from the
packet's own section 5 minimum, omits material decision content
(ADR-SB-004 policy dimensions, ADR-SB-007 completion receipt, ConPort
never owns task state, historical-vs-current distinction, open-loop
event kinds). Repairing it means re-freezing the denominator, which
supersedes the freeze at a9397e5630 and is an operator decision.

Also records three failed audit routes before the working one, and the
prompt/head discrepancy the auditor itself detected. The prompt was not
rewritten to match the head it audited; editing it would falsify custody.

Every commit after C1 touches only proof/ and task-packets/, so the
audit binding on 7955ef33d7 stays valid.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

proof(second-brain): record the embedded-audit representation gap truthfully

Once PROOF.json existed, the change-contract preflight and the pre-commit
proof hook required a top-level embedded_audit block. No truthful block
is constructible for this audit route.

schemas/proof/embedded_audit.schema.json is strictly binary: SKIPPED
requires auditor_tool 'none' and auditor_model 'unknown'; any other
status forbids both. Its enums cannot name the grok CLI that actually
ran. The two representable options are therefore to claim the audit was
SKIPPED — falsely asserting no audit happened, hiding a FAIL verdict —
or to pick a tool and model from the enum, fabricating an auditor
identity, which packet section 19 forbids.

Neither was used. The block records status FAIL, which is true and
representable, keeps honest fallback values for the two fields the
schema cannot express, and states the limitation in skip_reason. Three
error strings, one cause; the eight findings were converted to the
schema's finding object shape and validate.

The gate fails because this packet refuses to overstate its audit. A
packet that fabricated auditor_tool claude-code-cli would have passed it
while lying about who audited it.

Schema repair is out of scope: packet section 1 forbids embedded-audit
platform repair.

message:
proof(second-brain): C0_REFREEZE — supersede the incomplete coverage denominator

The first independent audit returned FAIL with 3 blockers and 5 must-fix
findings. MUST_FIX 1 established that the 97-clause denominator was
materially incomplete, and BLOCKER 2 established why: its declared
authority was TASK_PACKET_SECTION_5_MANDATORY_COVERAGE, and §5 calls
itself a minimum. The packet's own framing is not the audited authority.
That is also how "dopeTask" — a string that appears nowhere in the
candidate — became a canonical authority value.

This commit replaces the denominator and nothing else. It touches no file
under schemas/second_brain/contracts/ and no validator, because a freeze
that arrives alongside the artifacts it constrains proves nothing about
ordering; git history is the proof.

Authority: operator ruling of 2026-08-12, authorizing the re-freeze and
reproduced verbatim in DENOMINATOR_REFREEZE_RECEIPT.json so the pin the
validator will carry has an on-repository authorization record.

Census: every normative unit of the candidate is disposed of in
DENOMINATOR_CENSUS_WORKSHEET.json — mapped to clause IDs or excluded with
the operator's DO-NOT-INCLUDE reason. 160 clauses (was 97): 63 added, 86
modified, 11 unchanged, 0 removed. All six omissions the auditor named by
hand are present and are checked by name at generation time.

Two structural changes carry most of the repair:

- Fragment provenance. "Vector-first answer generation" is verbatim
  candidate text, so a clause could have cited a *rejected* design as its
  own grounding. Every fragment must now fall inside its ADR's Context /
  Proposed decision / Consequences span.
- Testable rule shapes. REQUIRE/MUST_EXIST with a label like
  PURGE_DEPENDENCY_GRAPH states that something is named, not that
  anything must be true. No remaining shape can carry an opaque token.

The superseded freeze at a9397e5630 stays in history and is not described
as valid in hindsight. It is the denominator the first audit proved
incomplete.

Refs: TP-DMX-SECOND-BRAIN-ADR-CONTRACT-EVIDENCE-001, PR #1227

message:
fix(second-brain): close the audit finding class in one wave

The first independent audit returned FAIL with 3 blockers and 5 must-fix.
The operator authorized repairing the whole class in one wave rather than
patching finding by finding, which is what keeps review carousels turning.

Structural repairs, not removals:

- BLOCKER 1. The re-frozen denominator's sha256 is const-pinned in the
  validator. A post-freeze clause edit fails, and since every contract
  rule must equal its inventory clause, editing both sides consistently
  fails too — including for booleans, which have no text to check. The
  honest limit is stated in the source: a producer can edit the pin, but
  not quietly, because the pin, the receipt and the operator's verbatim
  ruling all move together.
- BLOCKER 2. `dopeTask` is gone. Authority values must appear verbatim in
  the cited candidate text; a named guard restates it across the clause
  set and every contract file.
- BLOCKER 3. Closed sets are compared against the deterministic
  tokenization of a verbatim source enumeration. Shrinking now fails
  exactly as widening does — dropping PURGE used to pass.
- MUST_FIX 2. Port operation catalogues and invented schema properties,
  enums and lifecycle states are deleted. Every remaining property name,
  enum member and const string is bound to a clause and a verbatim
  candidate phrase, recomputed at validation. Some names now read as
  candidate prose rather than as API names; that is the point.
- MUST_FIX 3. The four-way recall ranking is gone. authority-first is a
  boolean; the four source classes are a closed set with no order among
  the other three.
- MUST_FIX 4. No rule shape can carry an opaque label any more.
  PURGE_DEPENDENCY_GRAPH stated that something was named, not that
  anything had to be true.
- MUST_FIX 5. The FO-01 status record is checked as a whole projection of
  its receipt across 39 fields, non-receipt fields are pinned, the
  traceability matrix is required rather than skipped when missing, and
  every status leaf must be classified.

Two repairs came out of the census rather than the audit: a clause may no
longer be grounded in text from a Rejected alternatives section, because
"Vector-first answer generation" is verbatim candidate text; and the two
ADR-SB-009 types are no longer stated as named-type requirements, since
the candidate never names them.

FALSE_GREEN_MATRIX.json records all ten operator-mandated mutations
failing via their intended guard. Rows 9 and 10 are loops over all 63
added clauses and all 39 projected FO-01 fields — the ruling says "each",
so nothing is sampled. Half the suite re-pins the validator to the mutated
state first, so the freeze hash cannot take credit for a semantic guard's
work; that mode is what BLOCKER 1 survived.

Gates: validator 94/94, adversarial suite 63/63, packet schema PASS,
diff --check PASS. change-contract and pre-commit FAIL for one cause, the
embedded-audit representation gap, re-observed at this tree rather than
carried forward. Repairing that schema is out of lane per packet §1.

The independent audit is PENDING and controlling. PR #1227 stays a draft.

Refs: TP-DMX-SECOND-BRAIN-ADR-CONTRACT-EVIDENCE-001, PR #1227

proof(second-brain): independent audit PASS — 0 blockers, 0 must-fix

Round-2 audit of frozen head 6e1b4472ba, run in a fresh read-only session
in a throwaway detached worktree with no producer conversation history.
It verified the freeze chain from bytes rather than from the handoff:
that a9397e5630 holds the superseded 97-clause inventory and does contain
the invented authority token, that 3e0d89815c contains zero files under
schemas/ and no validator change, and that the live inventory hash equals
both the validator pin and the receipt.

Its adversarial work went past what was asked. It exercised all 19
SET_EQUALS clauses for both shrinking and widening, found no escape, and
scanned every leaf of the FO-01 status record for an unclassified field.

Two residual observations, neither a must-fix, both confirmed by the
producer and recorded with evidence in AUDIT_R2_RESIDUALS.json:

- The census worksheet labels 25 clauses UNCHANGED that the computed
  supersession record lists as modified. All 25 are rule-type renames
  under the new taxonomy with byte-identical machine values and
  operators. The two fields answer different questions and the
  worksheet's was left unstated. Not corrected in place: editing audited
  content after the audit is the recursion the post-C1 boundary exists to
  prevent, and the computed receipt is the authoritative record.
- With the validator's own pin and the receipt both rewritten, clause
  booleans that no Group S pin covers can be flipped while the validator
  exits 0. That limit was written into the validator header before the
  audit ran. The distinction that matters held: a consistent bilateral
  edit with the pin left alone fails at A09, which is the false-green
  round 1 found.

Round-1 audit artifacts are untouched. Round 2 uses AUDIT_PROMPT_R2.md
and AUDITOR_REPAIR_2_REPORT.md, the latter a name the embedded-audit
schema's report_path pattern already accepts, so recording this audit
introduces no second schema failure beside the known one.

The prompt was written after the freeze so it names the head it audited.
Round 1's named a head that had moved; the auditor caught it. This
ordering removes the failure mode rather than repeating it.

A first invocation was killed mid-run with no verdict; it is recorded in
the custody file rather than dropped, and both worktrees were verified
unmodified before the re-run.

Gates unchanged: validator 94/94, suite 63/63, matrix 10/10. The
change-contract finding is now a single record naming two fields, both
the embedded-audit representation gap. A PASS does not turn that green
and was never going to.

Terminal verdict: READY_FOR_OPERATOR_CONTRACT_EVIDENCE_MERGE_DECISION.
Merge remains OPERATOR_ONLY. The PR stays a draft and no ADR disposition
changes.

Refs: TP-DMX-SECOND-BRAIN-ADR-CONTRACT-EVIDENCE-001, PR #1227

issue.title: feat(audit): admit the grok-cli/grok-4.5 embedded-audit route

repository.name: dopemux-mvp
repository.description: ADHD-aware cognitive ops stack for developers

issue.body:
The trusted embedded-audit contract had no vocabulary for the Grok runner: auditor_tool enumerated [agy, antigravity, claude-code-cli, copilot-cli, gemini-cli, pal-mcp-clink, none] and auditor_model enumerated [sonnet, claude-sonnet-4.6, opus, gemini, gemini-3.1-pro-high, unknown], with zero grok entries, additionalProperties false, and allOf[1] forbidding tool 'none' or model 'unknown' for any non-SKIPPED status. A completed, passing Grok audit therefore had exactly two representable encodings, both false: claim SKIPPED (asserts no audit happened) or name a runner from the enum (fabricates an auditor identity). The gap was recorded rather than papered over in proof/TP-DMX-SECOND-BRAIN-ADR-ACCEPTANCE-001-AC2-AMENDMENT/GROK_SCHEMA_REPRESENTATION_GAP.md, which scoped this packet.

This fixes the vocabulary instead of teaching the evidence to lie. It admits exactly one pair, grok-cli / grok-4.5, bound fail-closed in both directions so neither half can be stated without the other, following the existing gemini-3.1-pro-high/agy precedent and closing that precedent's one-directional gap for the new pair. grok-4.5-build is deliberately excluded as a usage/telemetry label rather than a requestable model id, and grok-4.6 (now the runner default) is excluded as outside the authorization.

Backward compatibility is proven at class level, not by sample: a differential test reads the pre-change schema from git and asserts old and new agree on the verdict for every pre-change tool/model pair across all five statuses. The full proof corpus revalidates 74/74 PASS under the new schema.

Scope was set by a deterministic consumer inventory, recorded in the proof bundle. scripts/audit/run_embedded_audit.py is deliberately NOT changed: it holds no auditor recognition table; its tool/model values come from normalize_pal_clink_audit_output (which always emits pal-mcp-clink) or pass through from an accepted local attestation, and its _skipped_audit helper correctly hardcodes the none/unknown pair. scripts/audit/local_audit_acceptance.py is likewise unchanged, being tool-agnostic and delegating to Draft7. The one consumer that did require a change is the parity corpus in tests/audit/test_local_audit_acceptance.py, which pins the conditional count and demands a violating fixture per conditional.

No runtime behaviour changes and no other packet's proof bundle is edited.

---

## Independent audit

AGY `gemini-3.1-pro-high`, frozen head `8290d7bd8e`, throwaway detached worktree, no producer conversation history. **Verdict PASS, findings None.**

**Bootstrap rule satisfied mechanically.** The packet that admits the Grok route must not be approved by Grok. This bundle's own `PROOF.json` validates under the **pre-change** schema as well as the new one, so the auditor identity never required the route being admitted.

Recorded rather than tidied: the auditor omitted the explicit BLOCKERS/MUST_FIX counters and the "what I could not verify" section, so zero/zero are marked DERIVED from "Findings: None" rather than auditor-stated. Two earlier route attempts produced no verdict and are recorded. AGY was re-probed for the canned-response failure another packet recorded earlier the same day and found functional on 1.1.12 before use.

## Validation

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `tests/audit/test_embedded_audit_grok_route.py` | 57 passed |
| `tests/audit/` | 379 passed |
| `validate_audit_proof.py --all proof` | 75/75 PASS |
| Intended #1227 block, new schema | PASS |
| Intended #1227 block, pre-change schema | FAIL (exactly the two enum reasons) |
| Negative control (conditional deleted) | 3 tests go red |
| pre-commit | 0 failed hooks |

## Not in scope

Does not merge or edit PR #1227, admit `grok-4.6` or `grok-4.5-build`, add Grok to the auto router, change runtime behaviour, or update docs (deliberately deferred).

**Note for future Grok audits:** the runner default moved to `grok-4.6` while this was written. Unpinned invocations will be unrepresentable — pin `-m grok-4.5`.

    AUDITED_FILES = 36
    DRIFTED_AUDITED_FILES = 0

Round 2 recorded the auditor model as UNKNOWN_TO_PRODUCER. That was truthful
at audit time and became insufficient the moment the proof had to NAME the
model. It is now established from evidence, not assumption: the runner's own
per-session metadata records grok-4.5 for both the completed run and its
killed precursor, and the timestamps corroborate the custody record's account
of a killed first attempt. Recorded as RUNNER_SESSION_METADATA_VERIFIED with
provider_attestation = UNKNOWN, in a new file.

The historical invocation is preserved exactly and NOT rewritten to add
-m grok-4.5. It never had a model flag. The invocation records what was
executed; the session metadata records what served it. Merging the two would
turn a true identity repair into fabricated execution history.

AUDIT_PROMPT_CUSTODY_R2.json and AUDITOR_REPAIR_2_REPORT.md are untouched.
Reconciliation adds a record; it does not revise one.

embedded_audit now truthfully reads PASS / grok-cli / grok-4.5, and the
representation gap is converted from active blocker to HISTORICAL_RESOLVED
against f0a0e839b4 — the historical fact that it existed is kept, because it
shaped how rounds 1 and 2 were reported.

Gates that were red for representation are now green:
    proof-embedded-audit-schema  FAIL -> PASS
    change-contract              FAIL(1 finding) -> PASS
    pre-commit                   2 failing hooks -> 0
    validator 94/94 · suite 63/63 · matrix 10/10 · packet schema · diff --check

No fresh contract audit: the vocabulary became representable, the audited
content did not change.
